tool: OTC English Check v1.0 — initial diagnostic, not an official exam
learner: DEMO-01 — fictional sample / 虛構示例

speaking.task: Describe a place where you like to study or spend time. Where is it? What do you do there? Why does it suit you? Give one specific example.
Describe a time when you learned something difficult. Who was involved? What happened? What changed afterwards? Explain what you would do differently next time.

writing.task: You cannot attend your study group this Friday. Write an email to the organiser. Explain why, ask what you will miss, and suggest how you can catch up. You may invent the details.
writing.response:
Dear Alex,
I am sorry that I cannot attend our study group this Friday because I have a appointment at the same time. Could you tell me which chapters the group will discuss? I can read them on Saturday and send my notes to you. If there is any group work, please let me know how I can help from home. Thank you for your understanding.
Best wishes,
Sam

writing.task: Some students prefer to study alone; others prefer to study with a group. Which approach works better for you? Explain your view with reasons and a specific example. You may also mention a limitation of your preferred approach.
writing.response: I prefer studying with a small group because I can ask questions when I do not understand an idea. Other students sometimes explain the same topic in a different way, which helps me remember it. Last month, my friends and I prepared a presentation about public transport. I understood the reading, but I was not sure how to organise my part. One friend suggested three main points, and I practised explaining them to the group. Their questions helped me notice where I needed more detail. However, group study is not always efficient. We sometimes talk about unrelated things and lose time. For this reason, I think everyone should prepare alone first and agree on a clear task before meeting. This make our group more useful and gives quieter students time to think.
